description:
FILED s536 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-08) on the USER's direction (paraphrased): correctness first, so #4061 stays; a serious benchmarking effort on what is slow in real programs is to come later.

NOT SCHEDULED: the USER names the session.  What it is: measure where TIME goes in REAL programs (the everyday corpus, the CPAN board's test suites, Rosetta, a few real applications), end to end and by profile (SBCL statistical profiler over the compiled run, the compile phase separately), and rank the levers by measured gain in ABSOLUTE time (Target A, feedback_speed_absolute_not_ratio) -- not more micro rows in tools/bench-exec.pl.

KNOWN INPUTS to carry into it:
- #4061 (s532d, MAIN-READY-75): every bless writes *p-rebless-stash* (an SBCL weak hash table, synchronized, ~220 ns per write -- scratch/s532d/wt.lisp in the s532d worktree); INFO rows arrobj-new 0.2880 -> 0.5513 (1.9x) and refarr-x 0.0849 -> 0.1954 (2.3x, `ref []` once any array is blessed).  The four ruling rows (methret, json-rt, moo-objs, mapmulti) are in noise.  The representation alternative (the class carried by the referent itself rather than a weak side table) is the lever to measure here.
- docs/method-lookup-eval-s534.md (#4523-#4525): inherited method calls 3.9-7.4x perl, a USER decision pending.
- docs/speed-review-s509.md: start-up and the thirteen slow bench rows profiled then.
- docs/where-the-time-goes.md, docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md: the earlier worklists.


=== INPUT (s536b, 2026-11-08) === #4305 (the @{} / %{} dereference overloads, one resolver %p-deref-overload): in a program with NO deref overload the cost is nil (refderef +0.2 %); once ANY class registers @{} or %{}, every dereference of an UNBLESSED ref goes through the overload lookup -- refderefov 0.1247 s -> 0.2408 s (+93 %).  Lever named by the agent: a per-class "has a deref overload" bit, or the pending method / overload cache (#4523-#4525).  Correctness kept (the USER's s536 ruling).

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === The USER asked for it in two tasks: #4787 (the CPAN distributions run under perl and PCL, time compared file by file, the list of what should be faster) and #4788 (a review of the rest of PCL for low-hanging speed fruit).  This task stays as the umbrella and the list of known inputs.

=== INPUT (s538b, MAIN-READY-89, 2026-11-13) === #2371 DESTROY at program exit: a program WITH a non-empty DESTROY / AUTOLOAD anywhere pays ~22-35 ns per bless (the weak-vector registration; bench rows blessnew-d +7.4-8.5 %, blessdes +5.5 %); a program with none pays one defglobal read (blessnew in the noise).  Global destruction of 100,000 live objects: 0.052 s (perl 0.017 s).  Correctness kept (the USER's s536 ruling).

=== INPUT (s540b, 2026-11-13) === docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md: nine low-hanging levers filed (#4981-#4985, #4988-#4991) and the bigger items with what they wait for; the largest single find is #4981 (tr/// re-expands per call: a Data::Dumper program 7.12 -> 0.59 s).


=== s540a (2026-11-13) === The board half done: docs/cpan-speed-comparison-s540.md (#4787) -- PCL board time is 82 % loading; the ranked list filed as #4961-#4967 (+ #4986); #4061 and #4305 are NOT visible at board scale.
=== s540 (2026-11-13) === #4787 and #4788 are DONE (docs/cpan-speed-comparison-s540.md: the board is 33x perl in CPU and 82 % of it is load; docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md: nine levers).  The USER then asked for the board measurement to be redone for the RUN PHASE only: #4791 (after s540d merges).
subject: LATER (USER s536): serious benchmarking of what is SLOW IN REAL PROGRAMS -- profile ordinary programs and CPAN suites end to end, not micro rows; inputs include #4061's weak-table cost (arrobj-new 1.9x, `ref []` after any array bless 2.3x)
